hook: The Norwegian who was first to the South Pole and first through the Northwest Passage.

pages.x: Roald Amundsen was born in 1872 in Borge, Norway, into a family of shipowners. His mother wanted him to be a doctor, but he dreamed of the poles, and slept with his windows open in winter to toughen himself up.

In 1897 he sailed on the Belgica, the first ship to spend a winter in the Antarctic, trapped in the pack ice. The crew fell ill with scurvy, and he helped save them by feeding them raw seal and penguin meat.

From 1903 to 1906, with six men in a little fishing boat, the Gjøa, he became the first to sail the Northwest Passage over the top of North America. He spent two winters with the Netsilik Inuit, learning to drive dogs and dress in furs.

In 1910 he set off, saying he was going to the North Pole. But the North Pole had just been claimed, so he secretly turned south, told his crew at Madeira, and sent the British explorer Scott a telegram: he was heading for Antarctica.
With four men, 52 dogs and skis, he reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911, five weeks before Scott, and planted Norway's flag. Scott and his men died on their way back.
In 1926 he flew over the North Pole in the airship Norge. He and his companion Oscar Wisting became the first people to reach both poles.
In 1928 he flew off from Tromsø to search for his rival Umberto Nobile, whose airship had crashed in the Arctic. His plane vanished over the sea and was never found. Nobile was rescued.
Amundsen's careful planning and the skills he learned from the Inuit made him the greatest polar explorer of all.
pts: First to reach the South Pole
First to sail the Northwest Passage
Among the first to reach both poles
